messages:
incident-bot: P0 ALERT: API error rate spike detected for /v1/generate in us-west-2. Threshold breach at 1769501110. Automated page to oncall.

maria (oncall): seeing 502/504s and higher latencies from our gateway. Error percent ~18% over 5m. I'll join bridge.

sam (eng-sre): I'm on the bridge — grabbing logs from edge and runtime. Early guess: increased 429s from upstream redis cache and backend model instances hitting OOM retries.

lee (platform): alerting cloud provider — opening support case now. Case: AWS-17695XX submitted, requesting priority escalation. cc @ben for customer comms.

anna (support): customer impact: several mid-market tenants reporting failures in streaming responses. Badge: degraded. Draft status page update below — please tweak: "We're investigating increased errors and latency for model inference in us-west-2. Some requests may time out or return errors; we are working with our cloud provider and expected mitigations underway."

ben (pm): approve status page. Add recommendation: "If you rely on us-west-2, temporarily route traffic to eu-west-1 via our console as a mitigation."

maria (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) enable regional fallback routing to eu-west-1 for critical customers, 2) scale Dedicated pools in us-west-2 by +2 nodes (warm), 3) enable aggressive KV cache warming and bypass failing Redis cluster by switching to local ephemeral cache for reads for 10m.

sam (eng-sre): commands I'm running now:

```
# scale runtime pool
redwoodctl scale --region us-west-2 --pool inference-pool --add 2
# switch cache reads to local fallback
redwoodctl config set --key runtime.cache.read_fallback --value local_ephemeral --region us-west-2
```

sam (eng-sre): logs show Redis 8.2 cluster showing connection timeouts and increased CPU on host i-0abc123. Suspect upstream managed Redis (vendor) is degraded.

lee (platform): AWS response: "We observed a network hardware flapping event affecting a subset of instances in us-west-2; team is replacing host and rerouting traffic. Case updated: AWS-17695XX-ESCALATE. TAM engaged. ETA for remediation 20-30m." Pasting AWS SR snippet below: "We are actively replacing the underlying hardware and performing instance replacements; automatic recovery in progress."

anna (support): customer notification template (short): "We are investigating increased errors for inference in us-west-2. Our engineers have engaged the cloud provider and are applying mitigations (regional fallback, autoscaling). We will update within 30 minutes or when we have new info. Sorry for the disruption." Approve? :thinking: 

ben (pm): approve. Add "contact support if you need assisted failover" line.

maria (oncall): contacting top affected customers directly now. cc @anna for synched message. Also creating an internal notify for account execs.

sam (eng-sre): temporary workaround implemented: switched cache reads to local_ephemeral and added extra retry with jitter for model requests. Error rate dropped to ~6% in the last 5m.

incident-bot: status_page: UPDATE posted at 1769501230: "Investigating — mitigation in progress; working with cloud provider."

lee (platform): vendor comms: AWS TAM wants NTP logs and kernel oops; I'm collecting and attaching to the case. Also asked for instance replacement timeline. Keeping them on high priority.

sam (eng-sre): note for postmortem: correlate runtime OOM/retries with instance replacement events and cache failover. Capture test harness load during rolling deploys.

maria (oncall): handoff note for next oncall: we expect AWS to finish host replacements in ~20m; keep fallback routing enabled until stable for 30m after AWS reports OK. If error rate >10% escalate back to SRE lead.

ben (pm): customer comms cadence: initial notice (sent), update at 30m or earlier, final update & RCA within 72h.

anna (support): created parent ticket for affected customers with template and assigned to CSMs. Providing proactive offers for assisted failover.

aws-tam-bot: AWS SR update: "Host replacements complete for affected instances. Networking asynchronous resync in progress — monitoring. No additional impact expected. Case will remain open for verification."

sam (eng-sre): seeing gradual recovery in instance health; error rate down to 1.2% last 2m. Rolling back cache fallback to standard in 10m unless regressions.

maria (oncall): thanks team. I'll close bridge once metrics stable for 30m. Leaving these action items for postmortem: vendor escalation timeline, mitigation latency, status page wording, and customer outreach log.

ben (pm): adding note to product: check regional autoscale thresholds and failover UI to make assisted fallbacks easier.

anna (support): drafting final customer update template and will send once we confirm 30m stable state.

incident-bot: BRIDGE CLOSED at 1769501450 by maria (oncall).
